plan.title: Liver drug-treatment DE: DESeq2 3v3 with power assessment
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is which genes differ between 3 treated and 3 control human liver samples (12,000 genes, raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts) and how much confidence three replicates support. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 two-group procedure: first a blind sample-structure QC (vst PCA, distances, library sizes) to confirm grouping and flag outliers; then a minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, an explicit-reference-level design, the DESeq2 Wald test with Cook's-distance outlier flagging, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05. Because 3 replicates per group is the low-power regime, a second count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood) is run on the same filtered counts and the intersection of the two gene sets is reported as the high-confidence set; the report carries the MA and dispersion diagnostics, the p-value histogram, the power statement computed from the closed form (RNASeqPower/PROPER absent), and a reproducibility record. Gene-level counts are already provided, so tximport length-offset import is not possible; the plan states this limitation instead of substituting an invented offset.
